page: Microsoft Azure E2s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8573C processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading running at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions.

This instance does not include local storage, though it is Premium Storage capable for remote disk attachments, and it does not bundle complimentary public IPv4 addresses. In benchmark evaluations, the E2s_v6 demonstrates strong single-core performance, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 2149.0 and an average stress-ng single-core rating. However, because of its 2-vCPU limitation, multi-core performance is constrained, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 2641.0 and a poor multi-core stress-ng rating. Memory bandwidth is also relatively low, with uncached read speeds at 21.51 GB/sec and write speeds at 14.04 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E2s_v6 offers a low-cost entry point into Azure's memory-optimized tier, providing a dense memory allocation relative to its compute resources. This makes it suitable for workloads that require a larger memory footprint but do not demand intensive multi-threaded CPU processing. Recommended workloads include small-scale databases, caching layers like Redis, lightweight web serving, and basic text or image processing tasks.
